name: Order Sample Compression
definition: The **Order Sample Compression** of $\mathcal{H}$ is the minimum size of a labeled compression scheme compatible with a well-order of its decoded hypotheses: each sample is decoded to the least compatible hypothesis and compressed by a minimal teaching set relative to earlier hypotheses.
graph_summary: Smallest labeled compression scheme compatible with an order of decoded hypotheses.

monotonic.proof: Restrict an order sample-compression scheme for $\mathcal H$ to samples realizable by a subfamily $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$. The same ordered decoded hypotheses, compressor, and decompressor remain valid (improper reconstruction is allowed), with no larger compression set. Thus $\mathrm{OSC}(\mathcal G)\leq\mathrm{OSC}(\mathcal H)$.

p_monotonic.proof: Darnstädt--Doliwa--Simon--Zilles prove that the order-compression number cannot increase under a coordinate projection; their proof projects an order scheme while preserving its compression size.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.
